entries.snippet: 3.1 The $B$-orbits on $G/B$ are the sets $B\cdot(gB)=\{bgB:b\in B\}$ of left cosets, that is exactly the double cosets $BgB$ of $B$ in $G$. By [F4] the double cosets $BgB$ are exactly $BP_{\mathrm{id}}B=B$ and $BP_sB$; so the two $B$-orbits of step 2.1 are these two cells, the orbit $\{\langle e_1\rangle\}$ corresponding to the identity and the complement $\{\langle e_2+ae_1\rangle:a\in\mathbb F_q\}$ to $s$. [given, F4, step 2.1]

entries.snippet: [F2] For $n\ge1$ the normaliser $N$ of $T$ consists of the monomial matrices, $\sigma\mapsto P_\sigma T$ is an isomorphism $S_n\to W=N/T$, and $\ell(\sigma)$ is the number of inversions of $\sigma$, so that $\ell(\mathrm{id})=0$; for a composition $\alpha$ of $n$ the standard parabolic is $P_\alpha=L_\alpha\ltimes U_\alpha$ with the entry criteria $\operatorname{blk}_\alpha(k)>\operatorname{blk}_\alpha(l)$ for $P_\alpha$, $\operatorname{blk}_\alpha(k)\ne\operatorname{blk}_\alpha(l)$ for $L_\alpha$ and $k\ne l$, $\operatorname{blk}_\alpha(k)\ge\operatorname{blk}_\alpha(l)$, $g_{kk}=1$ for $U_\alpha$ ([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]], [[def-compositions-partial-flags-and-standard-parabolics]], [[thm-levi-decomposition-of-standard-parabolics-in-gl-n-fq]]).

entries.snippet: 1.6 **The normal form of an arbitrary permutation.** Let $\sigma\in S_n$ and put $m:=M(\sigma)$. For all $i,j$ the sets $S_{ij}:=\{\,x\in J_j:\sigma(x)\in I_i\,\}$ and $T_{ij}:=\{\,x\in J_j:\sigma_m(x)\in I_i\,\}$ satisfy $|S_{ij}|=|T_{ij}|=m_{ij}$, and $S_{i1},\dots,S_{ir}$ as well as $T_{i1},\dots,T_{ir}$ partition $J_j$. Let $v\in S_n$ be the permutation which maps each $S_{ij}$ increasingly onto $T_{ij}$; it is well defined, and $v\in W_\beta$ because $v^{-1}(J_j)=J_j$ for every $j$. Let $u:=\sigma\circ v^{-1}\circ\sigma_m^{-1}$. Then $u\circ\sigma_m\circ v=\sigma$, and $u\in W_\alpha$: for $y\in I_i$ write $y=\sigma_m(w)$ with $w\in J_j$, so that $w\in T_{ij}$, hence $v^{-1}(w)\in S_{ij}$, hence $u(y)=\sigma(v^{-1}(w))\in I_i$. Therefore every $\sigma\in S_n$ satisfies $\sigma=u\,\sigma_{M(\sigma)}\,v$ with $u\in W_\alpha$ and $v\in W_\beta$. [construct, L2, L6]

entries.snippet: [L3] For $x\in M_n(\mathbb F_q)$ and $1\le i,j\le n$ let $r_{i,j}(x)$ be the rank of the submatrix on the rows $i,\dots,n$ and the columns $1,\dots,j$. Then $r_{i,j}(bx)=r_{i,j}(x)=r_{i,j}(xb)$ for $b\in B$, if $x\in BP_\sigma B$ then $r_{i,j}(x)=\#\{\,k\le j:\sigma(k)\ge i\,\}$, and the rank matrix $(r_{i,j}(x))_{1\le i,j\le n}$ determines $\sigma$ and hence the double coset $BxB$ ([[lem-rank-matrices-determine-the-pivot-permutation]]).

out_of_lane_findings.snippet: 1.6 **The normal form of an arbitrary permutation.** Let $\sigma\in S_n$ and put $m:=M(\sigma)$. For all $i,j$ the sets $S_{ij}:=\{\,x\in J_j:\sigma(x)\in I_i\,\}$ and $T_{ij}:=\{\,x\in J_j:\sigma_m(x)\in I_i\,\}$ satisfy $|S_{ij}|=|T_{ij}|=m_{ij}$, and $S_{i1},\dots,S_{ir}$ as well as $T_{i1},\dots,T_{ir}$ partition $J_j$. Let $v\in S_n$ be the permutation which maps each $S_{ij}$ increasingly onto $T_{ij}$; it is well defined, and $v\in W_\beta$ because $v^{-1}(J_j)=J_j$ for every $j$. Let $u:=\sigma\circ v^{-1}\circ\sigma_m^{-1}$. Then $u\circ\sigma_m\circ v=\sigma$, and $u\in W_\alpha$: for $y\in I_i$ write $y=\sigma_m(w)$ with $w\in J_j$, so that $w\in T_{ij}$, hence $v^{-1}(w)\in S_{ij}$, hence $u(y)=\sigma(v^{-1}(w))\in I_i$. Therefore every $\sigma\in S_n$ satisfies $\sigma=u\,\sigma_{M(\sigma)}\,v$ with $u\in W_\alpha$ and $v\in W_\beta$. [construct, L2, L6]
